# Recall: what earlier work on this repository left

Spend in proportion to what missing an earlier ruling would cost. Match before reading anything whole. A log's first lines name its topic and its repository. A search for this repository's name or paths finds the Manifests that mention it. Open the few most relevant for work that settles a design or a decision, and fewer for a small, contained change. For pull requests, list the recent ones that touched the paths this topic concerns in one query. Read only the "Debt left" section of those that have one. When nothing overlaps, recall is done.

- **The workflow's own logs and Manifests** under `~/.manifest-dev/` on an overlapping topic: logs whose recorded repository is this one, and Manifests that name it or its paths. Read only the leading conclusions, rulings, and out-of-scope calls of those opened, never whole logs. Skip any recorded for another repository.
- **Debt any runner can see** — open Tickets in the project's Ticket store that concern the paths or area this topic touches, and the debt lines of recently closed ones, the "Debt left" sections of recent pull requests that touched the paths this topic concerns where the host can reach the forge, and recipes the project's verification harness lists `stale` (the harness is its one command for checking its result, with a recipe per feature, skill, document walk or eval suite; `list` shows each recipe's status). Without pull requests, tickets and local logs are what there is.

Carry each as a dated lead from an earlier session, to check before relying on it — never as verified evidence. An open Ticket's status settles whether its own work is done; debt lines on a closed Ticket stand until checked against the current code. Local logs are a personal cache that another runner or teammate never sees, so a ruling found only in one, and not already a decision record or a Taste entry, is offered for capture: as a decision record through the ADR offer when project docs are loaded, otherwise offered in the read for capture as a decision record, written on acceptance per the project's `docs/adr/CONVENTIONS.md`, or the `ADR_FORMAT.md` beside this file where it has none. In team mode, what local logs hold reaches the operator only, never Slack.

**Debt on the path.** When this topic's work will touch an area with recorded debt, check each item against the current code — a lock re-run, a flagged comment still there, a ticket's status — and offer to fold the items still standing into the work as a preparatory slice: make the change easy, then make the easy change. Leave debt off the path where it is. Declines are not recorded; the check keeps a repeated offer real.

**Hotspots.** When one area carries debt from several earlier runs, say so in the read with the count, and propose a dedicated topic — a structural refactor, or a paved path for that kind of work. The user rules on it; once accepted it runs through the same flow.

Where define runs this before encoding a Manifest, "the read" is its digest, and debt still standing on the path becomes, or joins, the preparatory slice its Deliverables cut. When figure-out already ran this in the same session, define carries that recall forward rather than repeating it or its offers.
